claims.text: Thin tungsten interlayers at HEA multilayer interfaces will promote a transition from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep at high temperature.
The initial HEA multilayer has coherent interfaces between adjacent HEA layers.
A thin, well-bonded tungsten layer can be incorporated at each HEA multilayer interface.
The resulting tungsten/HEA interfaces will be coherent.
Tungsten has a high melting point.
Tungsten has relatively low atomic diffusivity under the proposed creep conditions.
Tungsten interlayers act as diffusion barriers in HEA multilayers.
The diffusion-barrier action of tungsten suppresses diffusion-mediated creep.
Tungsten is sufficiently compatible with HEA compositions to facilitate coherent interface formation.
Coherent tungsten/HEA interfaces promote efficient dislocation nucleation.
Coherent tungsten/HEA interfaces promote efficient dislocation transmission.
Suppressing diffusion while promoting dislocation activity shifts the dominant creep mechanism toward dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Tungsten-containing multilayers will have lower creep rates associated with diffusion than otherwise identical multilayers without tungsten.
Tungsten-containing multilayers will exhibit increased dislocation activity at their interfaces.
Tungsten interlayers will improve the overall high-temperature creep strength of HEA multilayers.
Diffusion-controlled creep dominates in the corresponding HEA multilayers without tungsten under identical conditions.
The beneficial effect will occur primarily over a temperature-and-stress range in which diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep compete.
An excessively thick tungsten layer may weaken the mechanism shift or introduce brittleness.
